live_high.text: Fuchse Berlin to win the money line at 1.68 (-147) against RK Partizan AdmiralBet in Group A on Thursday 29 October, 18:45 CET at the Max-Schmeling-Halle. Berlin sit second on six points from 3-0-2, scoring 184 and conceding 172, while Partizan are fourth with one point from 0-1-4 after scoring 148 and conceding 184 in the same five rounds. The Serbian side have lost four of five and carry the weaker goal difference by 36, and the five points between the clubs in the same group make the 1.68 price on the hosts the selection here rather than the draw the tip split favours.

Take Sporting Clube de Portugal to win at 1.65 (-154) when they visit GOG at Arena Svendborg on Thursday evening (18:45 CET) with Group D carryover points at stake. Unbeaten group leaders Sporting (4-1-0, 9 points, 191:165, +26) boast the highest-scoring attack in the competition at 38.2 goals per game, paced on Thursday by Francisco Costa's personal Champions League record 14 goals from 16 shots alongside brother Martim Costa in a 42:40 win over Kristianstad, having already beaten GOG in Lisbon in Round 1. Second-placed GOG (3-1-1, 7 points, 178:172) needed a buzzer-beating Kevin Moller save to salvage a 33:33 draw at Szeged after surrendering a 6:0 late run. Sporting to win is the pick.

live_high.text: Back MT Melsungen to win at 1.54 (-185) in Wednesday's Group B trip to SC Jane Sandanski in Skopje (18:45 CET). Melsungen sit second in Group B on 6 points (3-0-2, 138:138) with a Main Round berth on the line after defeating group leaders Wisla Plock 28:26 in Round 5 with goalkeeper Nebojša Simić making three consecutive saves in crunch time and six goals apiece from Eric Balenciaga (6/6) and Aaron Mensing. Fourth-placed HC Vardar 1961 (1-0-4, 2 points, 154:158) are already eliminated from Main Round contention despite upsetting Nantes 33:27 behind Leon Ljevar's 7/9 shooting, and Melsungen already beat Vardar at home in Round 1. Melsungen to win is our call.

live_high.text: Back KS Kielce on the money line at 1.68 (-147) in the EHF Champions League Group F match against Kolstad on Wednesday 28 October, 20:45 CET at Hala Legionow. The competition's group table has Kielce second on six points from 3-0-2 with 155 goals scored and 153 conceded, while Kolstad are bottom and still without a win at 0-0-5, having scored 143 and conceded 178 across their five defeats. That is a 35-goal deficit over five rounds for the visitors, and the two sides are separated by six points in the same group, so the home win at 1.68 is the value rather than the draw that the listing's tip split leans towards.

Back Dinamo Bucuresti to win at 1.70 (-143) in Thursday night's Group E finale at FDI Stadium in Montpellier (20:45 CET). Third-placed Dinamo (1-1-3, 3 points, 134:145) remain alive for the second Main Round berth after dismantling SAH - Aarhus 37:23 on Wednesday — the biggest Champions League victory in club history — led by Victor Iturizza (5/5), Haniel Langaro, and goalkeeper Ionut Iancu, and Dinamo also won the Round 1 meeting in Bucharest. Fourth-placed Montpellier (1-0-4, 2 points, 150:165) have lost four straight and are already eliminated following Thursday's 40:34 defeat at Barca, where centre back Pol Valera noted mounting player injuries and Benjamin Richert received a direct red card. Dinamo Bucuresti to win is our selection.

live_high.text: Aalborg Handbold to win at 1.71 (-141) is the selection for Wednesday night's Group C top-spot showdown at Stade Pierre de Coubertin in Paris (20:45 CET). Unbeaten Aalborg lead Group C on 9 points (4-1-0, 170:145, +25) after defeating RK Celje 34:30 in Round 5 while rotating their bench behind Thomas Arnoldsen (6/8) and Juri Knorr, and the Danish champions already beat Paris Saint-Germain in Round 1 at Aalborg. Second-placed PSG (3-1-1, 7 points, 182:157) let a four-goal half-time lead slip in Wednesday's 29:28 defeat at eliminated HC Zagreb despite Ferran Sole's 10/11 outing, struggling against Zagreb's second-half 5-1 defence. Back unbeaten Aalborg on the money line.

live_high.match: SC Magdeburg vs HC Kriens Luzern
live_high.text: Back SC Magdeburg to win the money line at 1.68 (-147) in the EHF Champions League Group F meeting with HC Kriens-Luzern on Wednesday 28 October, 20:45 CET at the GETEC Arena. The competition's own group table, read on 24 October, has Magdeburg top on a perfect 5-0 with 176 goals scored and 140 conceded, ten points from five rounds. Kriens-Luzern sit on four points from 2-3, having scored 158 and conceded 161, so the Swiss side arrive with a negative goal difference while the hosts are winning by more than seven goals a game. Magdeburg have also had the tougher half of the schedule on paper and still come through unbeaten, which is why the home win at a shade under 1.70 is the selection rather than a handicap.

live_high.text: Take Orlen Wisla Plock to win at 1.64 (-156) in Wednesday's winner-advances EHF Champions League Group B finale against HBC Nantes at ORLEN Arena (18:45 CET). Plock, Melsungen, and Nantes sit locked in a three-way tie on 6 points through five rounds, with Plock holding top spot on a +5 goal difference (141:136) after edging Vardar 33:32 at home in Round 4 and battling Melsungen to a 28:26 road loss on Thursday despite four goals apiece from Frederik Bjerre and Sergei Mark Kosorotov. Nantes (-1, 142:143) collapsed 33:27 at home to previously winless Vardar in Round 5, with coach Gregory Cojean citing ongoing one-on-one finishing struggles. Plock at home are the pick.

live_high.selection: NY Rangers to win — money line
live_high.text: New York Rangers to win the money line against Los Angeles. The Rangers' six wins from six home games are the clearest reason to prefer them, although their two-game losing streak prevents this from being a carefree selection. Los Angeles arrive with a 2-5-2 overall record and 21 goals scored against 32 conceded; New York are 7-5-1 with a 41-36 goal balance. The Kings have been more competitive away, going 2-2-2, so the straight win is preferable to asking the Rangers to cover a handicap. No starting-goalie assumption is built into the recommendation.

live_high.text: Edmonton Oilers to win the money line against Detroit. Edmonton's 8-2-1 start and 49 goals in eleven games offer a stronger attacking foundation than Detroit's 4-4-3 record and 29 goals. There is a useful caution in the venue splits: the Oilers are only 3-2-1 at home, while the Red Wings are 1-1-2 away, so neither split supports treating this as a routine blowout. Both teams carry a one-game losing streak. Back Edmonton to win rather than extending the argument to a puck-line bet, where the evidence is less persuasive.
